description: Plant crops with minimum mechanical disturbance of the soil.
benefits: Protects soil structure, reduces erosion and helps maintain soil biological activity.
implementation: Use direct seeding or planting through existing crop residues or mulch.
suitable_conditions: Can be adapted to different farming systems when suitable equipment and weed-management practices are available.
cautions: Requires appropriate residue and weed management.
related_crops: Maize, wheat, barley, soybean, rice, pulses

description: Grow crops during periods when the main commercial crop is not occupying the field.
benefits: Protects soil, recycles nutrients, improves soil structure, suppresses weeds and increases organic matter.
implementation: Plant an appropriate cover crop between main cropping periods and terminate it before competition with the following crop.
suitable_conditions: Useful during fallow periods where sufficient residual soil moisture exists.
cautions: Select species according to climate, soil moisture and the following crop.

description: Grow different crop species in planned sequences rather than repeatedly growing the same crop.
benefits: Improves nutrient cycling, soil biodiversity and can reduce pest, disease and weed pressure.
implementation: Plan multi-season crop sequences using crops with different rooting patterns and nutrient requirements.
suitable_conditions: Adapt rotation to local climate, soil and market conditions.
cautions: Choose crops that are agronomically and economically suitable for the farm.

description: Increase the diversity of crops grown in sequences or associations.
benefits: Supports biodiversity and improves water and nutrient-use efficiency.
implementation: Use multiple crop species and suitable rotations or associations.
suitable_conditions: Adapt species combinations to local farming conditions.
cautions: Management becomes more complex when many crops are combined.

description: Leave suitable crop residues on the soil surface after harvest.
benefits: Reduces erosion, protects soil from rainfall and heat, improves infiltration and contributes organic matter.
implementation: Retain residues rather than removing or burning them, while maintaining sufficient biomass for soil protection.
suitable_conditions: Particularly useful where erosion or soil organic matter loss is a concern.
cautions: Balance soil-cover requirements with livestock-feed and other residue uses.

description: Maintain a protective layer of plant material on the soil surface.
benefits: Reduces evaporation, protects soil and improves water infiltration.
implementation: Use suitable crop residues or other locally available organic materials.
suitable_conditions: Useful where soil moisture conservation and erosion control are important.
cautions: Ensure the material does not introduce pests or diseases.
related_crops: All suitable field and horticultural crops

description: Add suitable organic materials to improve soil organic matter.
benefits: Can improve soil structure, nutrient retention and biological activity.
implementation: Use well-managed compost, manure or other suitable organic amendments.
suitable_conditions: Useful where soil organic matter is low and suitable organic materials are available.
cautions: Application rates and material quality should be appropriate for the soil and crop.

description: Manage organic and mineral nutrient sources together according to crop and soil requirements.
benefits: Improves nutrient availability while reducing unnecessary nutrient losses.
implementation: Use soil information, crop requirements and appropriate organic and mineral nutrient sources.
suitable_conditions: All farming systems with appropriate soil and crop information.
cautions: Avoid excessive fertilizer or amendment application.

description: Combine appropriate biological, cultural, physical and chemical pest-management methods.
benefits: Can reduce unnecessary pesticide use and support ecological balance.
implementation: Monitor pests and use control measures according to pest pressure and crop conditions.
cautions: Chemical products should be used only appropriately and according to local requirements.

description: Integrate trees with crops and/or livestock within agricultural systems.
benefits: Can support soil health, biodiversity, water management and farm resilience.
implementation: Select tree and crop combinations suited to local climate, soil and farm objectives.
suitable_conditions: Suitable where tree-crop or tree-livestock integration is agronomically appropriate.
cautions: Consider competition for light, water and nutrients.
related_crops: Crops suitable for local agroforestry systems

description: Capture and use rainfall to improve water availability for agriculture.
benefits: Can improve water availability and reduce runoff and erosion.
implementation: Use suitable farm-scale water harvesting structures according to local conditions.
suitable_conditions: Useful where rainfall is seasonal or water availability is limited.
cautions: Structures must be designed for local rainfall, soil and terrain.

description: Use practices and structures that reduce soil loss by water and wind.
benefits: Protects topsoil and reduces nutrient and organic-matter losses.
implementation: Combine vegetation cover with appropriate terraces, bunds, contour measures or other suitable structures.
cautions: Structures should be designed for local terrain and rainfall.

description: Manage livestock grazing intensity and timing to protect vegetation and soil.
benefits: Can reduce vegetation degradation and support grassland recovery.
implementation: Control grazing pressure and allow vegetation adequate recovery periods.
cautions: Stocking levels and grazing periods must match local pasture productivity.

description: Retain, reuse or appropriately manage crop residues instead of burning them.
benefits: Helps retain organic matter and nutrients and reduces loss of soil-protective material.
implementation: Use residues as mulch, soil cover, compost material or other appropriate farm uses.
suitable_conditions: Applicable where sufficient residue is available.
cautions: Residue use should consider livestock feed, pests and disease risks.
